slides.title: Copilot delivers in daily use, with beta accounts scheduling more jobs per hour and renewing more often than matched peers

claims.claim: Scheduling productivity rose 5.5 times as much as in matched accounts
evidence: +9 pp
Change in jobs per dispatcher-hour, 12 weeks: Beta accounts 0.11; Matched non-beta 0.02

claims.claim: Beta accounts were also more likely to renew within 90 days
evidence: +4 pp
90-day renewal rate: Beta accounts 0.97; Matched non-beta 0.93

claims.claim: Volunteers were larger and more active than the base, which makes these gains an upper bound until a wider rollout confirms them
evidence: Beta: 240 volunteer accounts over 12 weeks, averaging 8.1 seats against 6.2 for all accounts; dispatchers also self-reported 4.1 hours saved a week

slides.title: Routewise's AI is a real but modest threat, putting at most about $0.6M of new ARR a year at risk

claims.claim: New ARR at risk from the lower win rate against Routewise is at most about $0.6M a year
evidence: 1,560 new-customer deals a year where Routewise competes (60% of 2,600)
7 pp fall in win rate, from 44% in H1 2026 to 37% in Q3 2026
$5,878 first-year ARR of a new 6.2-seat Core account
$0.6M new ARR a year at risk, if AI explains the whole fall

claims.claim: An upper bound, and a third of the Sales memo's figure
evidence: The whole fall in win rate is blamed on AI, yet Routewise also offered 20% off the first year in Q3 2026
Recovering a third of deals lost to Routewise, as the Sales memo expects, would be worth about $1.93M a year
That view reads AI mentions in 31% of loss notes as the cause of the loss
Q4 2026 win rates, after the Q3 promotion, will show how much of the fall is AI

slides.title: Survey intent overstates demand: 46% said they would buy, but only 14% of beta accounts did when asked to pay

claims.claim: 46% said they would buy, but only 14% of beta accounts did when asked to pay
evidence: Said likely to buy (survey, n = 610): 0.46; Bought when asked to pay: 0.14
30% of stated intent turned into purchases
Paywall test: 120 beta accounts offered Copilot at $149 per account per month in the last four weeks of the beta; 17 bought

claims.claim: Two biases inflate the survey; one limits the paywall
evidence: Survey: only 6% of admins replied, and their accounts average 9.4 seats against 6.2 overall
Wording: "likely" and "very likely" both count, and neither commits anyone to pay
Paywall: a real purchase, but by volunteers who were larger and more active than the base, so even 14% is a ceiling
Survey: October 2026, 610 of 9,800 account admins

slides.title: At the paywall take-up, the add-on would bring about $2.5M of new ARR, under a third of the plan

claims.claim: At the paywall take-up, the add-on would bring about $2.5M of new ARR, under a third of the plan
evidence: New ARR: CPO plan (survey intent) 8; Paywall take-up 2.45
1,372 accounts buy: 14% paywall take-up × 9,800 accounts
$1,788 a year per account: $149 × 12 months
$2.5M new ARR in the first year, at most

claims.claim: Even $2.5M is a ceiling, not a base case
evidence: CPO plan: applies survey intent to all 9,800 accounts, though respondents were the most engaged 6% of admins
Paywall take-up: measured on volunteers who were larger and more active than the base, so the full base would buy less
Price step: a flat $149 is 30% more for a typical 6.2-seat account, and price is already the second churn reason

slides.title: Add-on buyers are the heaviest users, and inference would absorb 41% of the price for the average buyer

claims.claim: Inference would absorb 41% of the price for the average buyer
evidence: Inference cost per month: Top 10% of accounts 130.5; Add-on buyers 61.2; Mean account 32.4; Median account 17.1; Add-on price 149
Requests a month from beta Table 2 and the paywall test (buyers averaged 6,800); cost = requests × $0.009 under the current contract

claims.claim: A flat fee per account attracts the costliest accounts
evidence: Add-on buyers: 1.9 times the requests of the mean account
Top 10%: make 58% of requests; inference eats 88% of the price
No relief before 2028: the rate is fixed to December 2027

slides.title: A Pro tier is the better package
Moving a third of accounts to Pro, as in 2023, would add about $2.9M of ARR and meet the NRR target

claims.claim: Moving a third of accounts to Pro would add about $2.9M of ARR and meet the NRR target
evidence: 3,234 accounts move to Pro: 33% of 9,800, the share that took the 2023 tier
$893 more ARR a year per account: 6.2 seats × $12 × 12 months
$2.9M new ARR in the first year, worth 5.0 percentage points of NRR

claims.claim: The estimate rests on four assumptions
evidence: A third of accounts move within a year, as 33% did when the last higher tier launched in 2023
Accounts that move have the 6.2-seat average; if larger accounts move first, ARR is higher
Lifting NRR from 101% to 105% needs about $2.3M of added net ARR on today's $57.6M
The lift lands in the 12 months after launch; holding 105% after that also needs lower churn (section 4)

claims.claim: Pro's ARR is about 18% above the add-on's best case, and grows with every seat

slides.title: A fair-use allowance of about 850 requests per seat a month keeps Pro within the company's margin floor

claims.claim: Typical accounts fit under the line; heavy users need a cap
evidence: Requests per month: Median account 1900; Mean account 3600; Add-on buyers 6800; Top 10% of accounts 14500
Pro breakeven 5,297
Median and mean: well below breakeven
Add-on buyers and top 10%: above it, so they need a cap

claims.claim: Allowance per seat a month 854
evidence: 5,297 requests ÷ 6.2 seats
$47.7 per Pro account a month can go to inference with company margin at 75%
$9 inference cost per thousand requests, fixed to December 2027
Breakeven: today's $44.93M gross profit + $2.89M Pro ARR − $0.6M running cost, less 75% of $60.5M revenue, leaves $1.85M a year for inference across 3,234 Pro accounts

claims.claim: Price overage above the cost per request
After 2027: list prices fell 35% in a year; a new contract lifts the line

slides.title: Of three ways to package Copilot, only a Pro tier is strong on revenue, margin and fit against Routewise

claims.claim: Free in Core: Rule out: about $3.81M a year of inference takes margin to about 70%
evidence: Price rise for a typical account: None
9,800 accounts × 3,600 requests a month × $0.009 × 12 = $3.81M of inference, plus $0.6M running cost, against $44.93M of gross profit on $57.6M

claims.claim: $149 add-on per account: Rule out: $2.45M at most, draws the heaviest users, reads as an extra charge
evidence: Price rise for a typical account: 30%

claims.claim: Pro tier, $12 more per seat: Recommend: most ARR, inside the floor with an allowance, same packaging as Routewise
evidence: Price rise for a typical account: 15%
Pro $12 ÷ $79 per seat

slides.title: The mobile delay is the launch's biggest risk: app reliability drives 4.5 times as much churn as AI features

claims.claim: App reliability drives 4.5 times as much churn as AI features
evidence: Main reason given by churned accounts, 2026, n = 1,190: Mobile app reliability 0.27; Price 0.22; Missing integrations 0.15; Went out of business or sold 0.14; Switched for AI features 0.06; Other 0.16
4.5x as much churn from mobile reliability as from AI features

claims.claim: Customers ask for a reliable app before AI
evidence: Mobile reliability: also the top request, with 38% ranking a reliable app first, twice the 19% for AI scheduling

claims.claim: AI features: a small churn reason, so Copilot's value lies in new deals and expansion, not in stopping churn
The delay: two more quarters on today's app leave the largest churn reason in place

slides.title: Beyond $1.5M of engineering, the launch's real cost is the mobile delay, with up to $1.1M of ARR at risk

claims.claim: $1.5M engineering, one-off, first half of 2027
evidence: 14 engineers for two quarters at $210,000 a year
Plus $0.6M a year to run Copilot
Repaid by about 17 months of Pro gross profit

claims.claim: 23% of the 60 engineers move to Copilot for two quarters
evidence: 46 engineers stay on the roadmap
No hiring assumed

claims.claim: $1.1M ARR at risk from mobile-related churn over the two-quarter delay (upper bound: half a year of it)
evidence: $57.6M ARR today × 14% annual logo churn × 27% of churned accounts name mobile reliability first = $2.2M ARR lost a year to mobile-related churn
Below the $2.89M a year Pro adds
Lost accounts do not come back
Upper bound: assumes churned accounts are average-sized and the rewrite would remove all mobile-related churn

slides.title: A gated plan launches Pro by mid-2027 and puts the Copilot engineers back on mobile the next quarter

evidence: Milestones: Go decision; Gate review; Contract ends
Copilot build: 14 engineers build and harden Copilot
Pro tier: Launch, then migration toward a third of accounts
